build.candidate: E12: borrow memory catalogue while deriving annotations

build_notes: The original release build completed in 7m 46s. A second invocation waited for its artifact lock, then verified the same build and saved the candidate binary.
A resume attempt used the wrong target directory and was interrupted before benchmarking; it produced no retained binary.

change.description: Compute reasons, symbol-link summaries and visibility against borrowed unchanged rows, release the lookup, then move rows into the response. Eliminates the complete catalogue clone without introducing a cache, API, schema or retrieval policy.
invariants: Keep original newest-first row order and retired-row behavior.
Resolve all dependency and refresh-target checks against the unchanged full catalogue.
Keep current source hashes, symbol-link summaries and transitive authorization.
Propagate dependency-decoding errors before returning records.
Keep the 20000-memory recall bound and existing E11-F1 freshness diagnostic unchanged.

decision: Retain for bounded filtered/disabled-request memory savings: peak RSS falls 22.5% and 25.9%. Ordinary and graph-assisted peak RSS rise 2.8% and 0.6%; latency changes are small. This is not a universal memory or speed improvement.
experiment: E12: borrow the memory catalogue while deriving annotations
limitations: Synthetic reviewed decisions over 40 tiny sources; no combined large source/memory qualification or independent user retrieval-quality claim.
Fresh CLI processes and warm OS cache, one excluded warmup per request/arm followed by five samples; both binaries get their own prepared graph cache at the same path.
The table pools 15 measured calls per workload/arm across three fixed probes; every per-probe median and raw sample is retained.
No builds, tests or other benchmark workloads were deliberately run alongside timed calls. Host-wide process listing was unavailable, so unrelated host load was not verified.
Prior full runtime and quality-gate results predate this change. E12 uses the 99 distinct focused tests and exact-response comparisons; full release qualification was not rerun.
Ordinary and graph-assisted recall still omit the oldest 5000 notes in the 25000-note fixture; source restoration still leaves E11-F1 stale freshness markers.

scale_comparison.limitations: Synthetic decisions over 40 tiny sources. Does not qualify combined large source/catalogue scale, independent real-user quality or warm-server latency. Existing oldest-memory omissions and the source-reversion freshness finding must remain identical.
scale_comparison.method: Per-binary caches prepared through pack in disposable stores, then parked by rename for same-path requests. Fresh CLI/measurement processes, warm OS cache, alternating arm/workload order and one excluded warmup. Complete context packets, citations, notes, omissions and all source/graph/memory/dependency/stale rows checked.
